title: Seihll yn obbyr
description: Ten short stories about people at work on the Isle of Man: a harbour assistant and a Dutch merchant, a court clerk at a trial, a virus laboratory, an archaeological dig at an old chapel, a farm worker, a shipyard reopened in Ramsey, an evening song class in Peel, a café cook at a christening party, glaziers at a tree garden, and a guide in the old Laxey mine.

lessons.title: Yn marçhan Ollanagh er y cheiy
lessons.summary: Theodora Bancroft, an assistant at the harbour office in Douglas, meets the Dutch merchant Joost Vermeulen on the quay; she speaks Dutch with him and finds storage for his packets of cheese, and he tells her that his business was in decline until a bank loan let him buy a ship, and that the increase in traffic on the quay is good for them both.
lessons.text:
Ta Theodora Bancroft ny cooneyder ec oik y phurt ayns Doolish. T'ee gobbraghey er y cheiy. Dagh moghrey, t'ee shooyl er y cheiy as t'ee coontey ny lhongyn as ny baatyn. Ta ram traaght er y cheiy 'sy tourey: lhongyn mooarey, baatyn beggey, gleashtanyn as sleih er dagh çheu. She obbyr y chooneyder dy freayll recortyssyn jeh'n traaght shoh ooilley.

Un moghrey, haink lhong veg veih Ollan stiagh 'sy phurt. Va marçhan er y lhong, Joost Vermeulen. Cha row agh beggan Baarle echey, agh va Ollanish ec Theodora. Va'n ayr eck ny Ollanagh, as v'ee loayrt Ollanish 'sy thie tra v'ee aeg.

“Moghrey mie,” dooyrt Theodora 'syn Ollanish. “Cre ta ayd er y lhong?”

Va taitnys mooar er y varçhan. “Ta paggadyn caashey aym,” dooyrt eh. “Ta keead paggad ayn. Ta mee laccal stoyral son ny paggadyn rish shiaghtin. Vel stoyral ayn er y cheiy?”

Va'n stoyral ooilley lane ec y phurt, agh va shamyr follym ec Theodora ayns thie shenn faggys da'n cheiy. Ren ny deiney ny paggadyn y ymmyrkey stiagh 'sy thie shen. Va ny paggadyn caashey sauçhey nish.

Lurg shen, ghow Theodora as y marçhan tey 'syn oik. “Va failleil 'sy chreck aym,” dooyrt Joost. “Va ny shappyn ayns Ollan kionnaghey caashey veih marçhanyn elley. Va'n failleil shen feer olk dou, as cha row argid aym son lhong noa. Agh hooar mee eeasaght veih'n vanc, as chionnee mee yn lhong shoh lesh yn eeasaght. Nish ta mee creck caashey ayns Ellan Vannin as ayns Nerin.”

“Ta bishaght 'sy traaght er y cheiy shoh neesht,” dooyrt Theodora. “Ta'n bishaght shen mie dooin ooilley. Ta obbyr ny smoo ayn son ny deiney er y cheiy, as ta caashey noa ayns ny shappyn.”

Tra hie yn lhong magh veih'n phurt, dooyrt y marçhan “gura mie ayd” 'syn Ollanish, as hug eh paggad caashey da'n chooneyder.

Feyshtyn:
C'raad ta Theodora gobbraghey?
T'ee gobbraghey ny cooneyder ec oik y phurt ayns Doolish, er y cheiy.
Cre'n fa va Ollanish ec Theodora?
Va'n ayr eck ny Ollanagh, as v'ee loayrt Ollanish 'sy thie tra v'ee aeg.
Cre va'n marçhan laccal?
V'eh laccal stoyral son keead paggad caashey.
C'raad hooar Joost argid son y lhong?
Hooar eh eeasaght veih'n vanc.
Vel bishaght 'sy traaght er y cheiy?
Ta. Ta bishaght 'sy traaght, as ta obbyr ny smoo ayn son ny deiney.

lessons.title: Yn cleragh 'sy chooyrt
lessons.summary: Lucinda Fairbrother, the clerk of the court in Douglas, writes down a trial: the prisoner Dorian Mallory, polite and calm, denies robbing a shop, the victim Wilberforce Tamblyn, an old shopkeeper unsteady on his feet, says a man came in suddenly and took the money, the judge listens to both, and when a picture from the shop shows the truth the prisoner stops denying the crime.
lessons.text:
Ta Lucinda Fairbrother ny cleragh 'sy chooyrt ayns Doolish. She obbyr y chleragh dy screeu dagh fockle ta ny briwnyn as ny deiney-leigh gra. T'ee lhaih neesht yn chassid roish dagh cooish. Ta'n obbyr trome, agh s'mie lhee eh.

Jeheiney shoh chaie, haink pryssoonagh aeg stiagh 'sy chooyrt, Dorian Mallory. Va'n pryssoonagh shoh cooyrtoil. Dooyrt eh “moghrey mie” rish y briw as rish y cleragh, as hass eh dy meen. Lhaih Lucinda yn chassid: “Ta kimmeeys er ve jeant. Va shapp ayns Doolish er ny roostey, as ta'n chassid noi'n phryssoonagh shoh.”

“Cha ren mee eh,” dooyrt y pryssoonagh dy cooyrtoil. Dobb eh yn kimmeeys. “Cha row mee ayns y shapp shen rieau.”

Eisht haink y dreih stiagh: Wilberforce Tamblyn, fer y shapp. Va'n dreih shenn as corragh er e chassyn, as ren y cleragh soiag y chur da. Agh va'n soiag corragh neesht, as hug ee soiag elley da.

“Va mee 'sy shapp 'sy fastyr,” dooyrt y dreih. “Dy doaltattym, haink dooinney aeg stiagh. Ghow eh yn argid ooilley veih'n chishtey, as roie eh magh. Va'n red ooilley feer doaltattym. Cha row traa aym dy loayrt.”

Ren y briw eaishtagh rish y dreih, as eisht ren eh eaishtagh rish y pryssoonagh. “Eaisht, Dorian,” dooyrt y briw. “She yn firrinys ta shin laccal 'sy chooyrt shoh. Vel oo obbal y kimmeeys foast?”

“Ta,” dooyrt y pryssoonagh. Agh eisht hug fer-leigh jalloo da'n vriw. Va'n jalloo shoh er ny ghoaill 'sy shapp, as va Dorian ry-akin ayn, lesh yn argid ayns e laue.

Lurg tammylt, loayr y pryssoonagh reesht. “Shoh yn firrinys,” dooyrt eh dy meen. “Ren mee yn kimmeeys. Cha row argid aym son bee.” Cha row eh obbal eh ny sodjey, as v'eh cooyrtoil derrey'n jerrey.

Hie Dorian dys y phryssoon son blein. Ren Lucinda screeu sheese dagh fockle, myr dagh laa. Ta'n firrinys ayns ny recortyssyn eck nish.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr ta ec Lucinda?
T'ee ny cleragh 'sy chooyrt ayns Doolish.
Cre'n kimmeeys va jeant?
Va shapp ayns Doolish er ny roostey.
Quoi yn dreih?
She Wilberforce Tamblyn, fer y shapp, yn dreih.
Cre'n fa hug Lucinda soiag elley da'n dreih?
Va'n chied soiag corragh.
Cre hug y fer-leigh da'n vriw?
Hug eh jalloo da'n vriw veih'n shapp.

lessons.title: Yn veerys 'sy scoill
lessons.summary: Rosalind Hepworth works in the hospital laboratory in Douglas, where her grandmother was a pioneer in the fight against tuberculosis; when many children at a school in Ramsey fall sick she tests samples, finds an infectious but not dangerous virus, explains to the head teacher Edmund Ashdown that the laboratory produces results quickly, and goes home to finish an academic paper, which she calls mental work.
lessons.text:
Ta Rosalind Hepworth gobbraghey ayns thie-lheeys mooar Ghoolish. T'ee ny oaylleeagh. Ta'n obbyr eck ayns shamyr veg lane dy ghreieyn, as t'ee jeeaghyn er veerysyn as er bacteyryn gorlagh. Ta ny bacteyryn gorlagh cur çhingys er sleih. Cha nel Rosalind lowal bee ny jough ayns y shamyr shen. Cha low ee red erbee ayns y shamyr nagh vel feme echey er.

Va shenn-voir Rosalind ny kioneraadagh. 'Sy vlein 1950, v'ee gobbraghey noi'n shymlee ayns Ellan Vannin. Va'n shymlee ny çhingys gowaltagh, as hooar ram sleih baase jeh. Hie ny kioneraadee shen magh dys dagh balley, as ren ad jeeaghyn lurg ny paitçhyn. Ta jalloo jeh'n chioneraadagh shoh ec Rosalind er y voalley 'syn oik eck.

Un moghrey, haink feysht veih scoill ayns Rhumsaa. Va 30 paitçhyn çhing. Va stiureyder ny scoill, Edmund Ashdown, goaill aggle. “Vel eh ny veerys gowaltagh?” dooyrt eh er y çhellvane.

Hooar Rosalind sampleyryn veih ny paitçhyn, as ren ee jeeaghyn orroo lesh ny greieyn eck. Ta ny greieyn shoh giennaghtyn freggyrtyn dy tappee. Ayns three ooryn, va'n freggyrt ayn.

“She veerys t'ayn,” dooyrt ee rish Edmund. “T'eh gowaltagh, as myr shen ta ny paitçhyn goaill eh veih y cheilley. Agh cha nel y veerys shoh feer olk. Lhisagh ny paitçhyn fuirraghtyn 'sy thie rish three laaghyn.”

Va taitnys er Edmund. “Ta mee lowal da dagh paitçhey çhing fuirraghtyn 'sy thie,” dooyrt eh.

'Sy fastyr, hie Rosalind thie as hoie ee sheese ec y voayrd. V'ee screeu pabyr acadoil mychione y veerys. She obbyr inçhynagh ta ayns screeu pabyr acadoil: cha nel oo gleashagh dty chorp, agh t'ou smooinaghtyn feer chreoi. Ta'n obbyr inçhynagh shoh slanjeant son Rosalind. Ta shamyr eck lesh soilshey mie: shen ynnyd slanjeant son obbyr. Lurg daa oor dy obbyr inçhynagh, hie ee dy cadley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr ta ec Rosalind?
T'ee ny oaylleeagh, as t'ee jeeaghyn er veerysyn as er bacteyryn gorlagh.
Quoi va ny kioneraadagh?
Va shenn-voir Rosalind ny kioneraadagh noi'n shymlee.
Row'n shymlee gowaltagh?
Va. Va'n shymlee ny çhingys gowaltagh.
Cre ta ny greieyn giennaghtyn?
T'ad giennaghtyn freggyrtyn dy tappee.
Cre va Rosalind screeu 'sy fastyr?
V'ee screeu pabyr acadoil mychione y veerys.

lessons.title: Fo'n euar ec y keeill
lessons.summary: The archaeologist Gwendolyn Pryor and her student Cuthbert Lyle dig at an old chapel under a yew tree near Ramsey: they find walls made with lime, sea shells from old meals, a skull in a grave, and a papal seal that may have belonged to a priest who came to the island in exile; she explains that the druid stories about the yew are only stories, and the finds go to the museum in Douglas.
lessons.text:
Ta Gwendolyn Pryor ny shenndaaleeagh. She shenndaaleeaght yn obbyr eck rish feed blein. 'Sy tourey shoh, t'ee kiaddey ec shenn keeill faggys da Rhumsaa, marish y studeyr eck, Cuthbert Lyle. Ta euar mooar ec y keeill. Ta'n euar shoh feer shenn, as t'eh freayll y keeill veih'n gheay.

Ayns y chied shiaghtin, hooar ad boallaghyn y keeill fo'n ooir. Va ny boallaghyn troggit lesh claghyn as eayl. “Va sleih jannoo eayl veih claghyn bane,” dooyrt Gwendolyn. “Ta'n eayl freayll ny claghyn ry-cheilley. Ta shenndaaleeaght ynsaghey dooin cre'n aght va sleih troggal 'sy traa shen.”

Ayns y nah hiaghtin, hooar Cuthbert ram shliggyn. “Cre'n fa ta shliggyn ayns shoh?” denee eh. “Ta'n traie foddey ersooyl.”

“Va bee ayns ny shliggyn shoh son y sleih shenn,” dooyrt Gwendolyn. “Ghow ad y bee veih ny shliggyn, as cheau ad ny shliggyn er y thalloo.”

Eisht, ayns oanluckey fo'n euar, hooar ad claigin. Ghow Gwendolyn y claigin ayns e laueyn dy meen. “She claigin dooinney eh,” dooyrt ee. “Va'n dooinney shoh shenn tra hooar eh baase.”

Faggys da'n chlaigin, va red beg cruinn. V'eh ny cowrey paabagh: cowrey veih Raue. “Va cowrey paabagh currit marish dy chooilley screeuyn veih Raue,” dooyrt Gwendolyn. “Foddee dy row y dooinney shoh ny saggyrt. Foddee dy daink eh dys yn ellan ayns eebyr. Va ram saggyrtyn ayns eebyr ayns ny shenn laghyn.”

Hooar Cuthbert skeeal mychione y keeill ayns lioar. “Ta'n lioar gra dy row druaight cummal fo'n euar,” dooyrt eh. “Va'n druaight shoh jannoo obbyr ny h-oie.”

Ren Gwendolyn gearey. “Ta ram skeealyn ayn mychione druaight erbee,” dooyrt ee. “Agh cha nel shenndaaleeaght geddyn red erbee jeh druaight ayns shoh. 'Sy feedoo cheead, ren sleih elley kiaddey ayns shoh, as cha dooar adsyn red erbee jeh druaight.”

Ec jerrey yn tourey, hie ny reddyn ooilley dys y tashtlann ayns Doolish. Nish ta'n claigin, ny shliggyn as y cowrey paabagh 'sy tashtlann, as ta sleih goll dys y tashtlann dy akin ad.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n obbyr ta ec Gwendolyn?
She shenndaaleeagh ee.
Cre va ny boallaghyn troggit lesh?
Va ad troggit lesh claghyn as eayl.
Cre'n fa va shliggyn faggys da'n keeill?
Va bee ayns ny shliggyn son y sleih shenn.
Cre hooar ad fo'n euar?
Hooar ad claigin ayns oanluckey.
C'raad ta ny reddyn nish?
T'ad 'sy tashtlann ayns Doolish.
Quoi ren kiaddey ayns shoh 'sy feedoo cheead?
Ren sleih elley kiaddey ayns shoh 'sy feedoo cheead.

lessons.title: Laa er y thie-ollee
lessons.summary: Ivor Penhale, a farm worker on Agatha Brightwell's farm near Sulby, starts work when the rooster crows; crows are a pest in the turnip field, he clears prickly gorse from the edge of the meadow and hurts his knee, and in the evening a hawk over the field drives the crows away while the horses stand in the paddock by the house.
lessons.text:
Ta Ivor Penhale ny obbree er thie-ollee Agatha Brightwell, faggys da Sulby. Dagh moghrey, ta'n kellagh cur eam roish y ghrian, as ta Ivor girree. Cha nel feme echey er clag: she yn kellagh y clag echey. “Ta'n kellagh shoh ny share na clag erbee,” ta Agatha gra.

Ta magher mooar dy napinyn ec Agatha. 'Sy tourey shoh, ta ram fannagyn çheet dys y magher napin. Ta ny fannagyn shoh ny paitt. T'ad goaill ny rassyn as t'ad brishey ny napinyn beggey. “Ta ny fannagyn ny paitt mooar,” dooyrt Agatha. “Cha nel mee abyl ad y lhiggey ersooyl.”

Ec oirr y magher, ta banjagh glass, as ta kirree ayns y vanjagh. Agh ta aadjin gaase er oirr y vanjagh, as t'eh goaill ny smoo dy ynnyd dagh blein. She obbyr Ivor 'sy laa shoh giarey yn aadjin. Ta'n aadjin jialgagh: ta birryn beggey er. Va Ivor giarey dy kiart, agh va'n aadjin jialgagh foast, as va fuill er e laueyn ec jerrey yn laa.

Lurg mean-laa, hie Ivor sheese er e ghlioon son giarey yn aadjin fo'n thalloo. Va clagh gheyre fo'n ghlioon echey, as hooar eh lhott. “Ta my ghlioon goll dy olk,” dooyrt eh rish Agatha. Ghow Agatha jeeaghyn er y ghlioon. “Cha nel eh feer olk,” dooyrt ee. “Agh ny jean obbyr er dty ghlioon son shiaghtin.”

'Sy fastyr, va Ivor as Agatha shassoo ec y thie. Dy doaltattym, haink shawk harrish y magher napin. Va'n shawk beg as tappee 'syn aer. Hie ny fannagyn ooilley ersooyl. “Ta'n shawk ny share na mish,” dooyrt Agatha, as ren ee gearey.

Faggys da'n thie, ta faaie veg, as ta daa chabbyl ayns y faaie. Hie Ivor dys y faaie as hug eh ushtey da ny cabbil. Eisht hie eh thie, as hug eh ushtey feayr er e ghlioon. Cha row'n kellagh cur eam nish, agh 'sy moghrey bee eh cur eam reesht.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa nagh vel feme ec Ivor er clag?
She yn kellagh y clag echey.
Cre'n fa ta ny fannagyn ny paitt?
T'ad goaill ny rassyn as brishey ny napinyn beggey.
Cre va Ivor jannoo er oirr y vanjagh?
V'eh giarey yn aadjin.
Cre haghyr da glioon Ivor?
Va clagh gheyre fo'n ghlioon echey, as hooar eh lhott.
Cre'n traa hie ny fannagyn ersooyl?
Hie ad ersooyl tra haink y shawk harrish y magher.
C'raad ta ny cabbil?
T'ad ayns y faaie veg faggys da'n thie.

lessons.title: Yn thie-obbree lhongyn ayns Rhumsaa
lessons.summary: Euphemia Garside leads the workers' society in Ramsey after the shipyard closes and two hundred men are left idle; two companies are merged into one, the government executive gives money so the merged company can revive the yard, an old worker, Bartholomew Crane, calls the deal a betrayal, but after she answers his question a majority of the workers votes for it and the yard opens again.
lessons.text:
Ta Euphemia Garside ny stiureyder er çheshaght ny obbreeyn ayns Rhumsaa. Rish keead blein, va thie-obbree lhongyn mooar ayns Rhumsaa. Agh blein er dy henney, va'n thie-obbree dooint, as nish ta daa cheead dooinney taaue. Cha nel obbyr erbee oc. T'ad shassoo er y cheiy, as t'ad jeeaghyn er y thie-obbree follym.

She keisht mooar ee shoh 'sy valley. Ta dagh peiagh loayrt mychione y cheisht. Ta'n cheisht scanshoil da dagh thie ayns Rhumsaa: cre'n aght vees obbyr ec ny deiney reesht?

'Sy tourey shoh, haink naight noa veih Doolish. Va daa cholught beg cochorpit ayns un cholught mooar. Lurg yn unnaneyssey shoh, va argid dy liooar ec y colught noa son troggal lhongyn. Va'n kiannoortys, reiltys yn ellan, son yn unnaneyssey. Ta'n kiannoortys laccal obbyr noa son ny baljyn beggey. “Ta'n colught noa laccal yn thie-obbree y aavioghey,” dooyrt Euphemia rish ny obbreeyn. “Ta'n kiannoortys cur argid da'n cholught cochorpit, as nee shin yn obbyr ooilley ayns Rhumsaa y aavioghey.”

Agh va obbree shenn, Bartholomew Crane, noi'n conaant. “She traartys eh!” dooyrt eh. “Ta'n colught noa shoh veih Sostyn. Cha bee ad eeck agh beggan argid dooin. She traartys noi ny obbreeyn eh.”

Ren Euphemia eaishtagh rish. “Ta keisht mie ayd,” dooyrt ee. “Agh vaik mee er y conaant. Bee ny obbreeyn er ny eeck myr roie. Cha nel traartys ayn. She obbyr eh, son daa cheead dooinney taaue.”

Ec jerrey yn çhaglym, ren ny obbreeyn reih. Va'n tromlagh son y conaant: daa cheead as nuy deiney, as cha row agh shiaght deiney noi. Va'n tromlagh feer vooar. Va Bartholomew noi foast, agh ghow eh rish y tromlagh.

Lurg three meeghyn, va'n thie-obbree foshlit reesht. Cha row ny deiney taaue ny sodjey. Ren y colught cochorpit yn thie-obbree y aavioghey, as va bea noa 'sy valley ooilley.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa ta ny deiney taaue?
Va'n thie-obbree lhongyn dooint, as cha nel obbyr erbee oc.
Cre haghyr da'n daa cholught beg?
Va ad cochorpit ayns un cholught mooar. Va'n unnaneyssey mie son Rhumsaa.
Cre dooyrt Bartholomew mychione y conaant?
Dooyrt eh dy nee traartys v'ayn.
Row'n tromlagh son y conaant?
Va. Va'n tromlagh feer vooar son y conaant.
Cre haghyr lurg three meeghyn?
Va'n thie-obbree foshlit reesht, as cha row ny deiney taaue ny sodjey.

lessons.title: Yn brastyl arraneyn ayns Purt ny h-Inshey
lessons.summary: Rosamund Treloar, a music teacher in Peel, leads an evening class of amateur musicians with a guitar, an old viol and a triangle; they sing from a reprint of an old Manx songbook in which asterisks mark the dialect words, she shows them how to sing the labial sounds with their lips, and at the end the creative student Silas Ingham brings a new song of his own, to everyone's joy.
lessons.text:
Ta Rosamund Treloar ny ynseyder kiaull ayns Purt ny h-Inshey. Dagh Jerdein 'syn oie, t'ee cur brastyl arraneyn Gaelg da kiaulleyderyn ancheirdagh. Cha nel ny kiaulleyderyn shoh gobbraghey lesh kiaull: t'ad nyn eirinee, nyn ynseyderyn as nyn obbreeyn oik. T'ad ancheirdagh, agh s'mie lhieu kiaull dy mooar.

Ta Silas Ingham cloie y gitar. Ta ben aeg cloie biol: shenn red jeh kiaull, feer chasley rish y gitar, agh t'ee cummal y biol er e glioon. Ta coraa dowin as bog ec y biol. Ta dooinney shenn cloie y troorane. Cha nel y troorane agh troorane beg yiarn, agh ta'n coraa echey glen as ard. “Ta'n troorane yn red smoo aashagh 'sy vrastyl,” ta'n dooinney shenn gra, as t'eh gearey.

'Sy vrastyl shoh, ta ny kiaulleyderyn goaill arraneyn veih lioar arraneyn shenn. Cha nel y lioar shoh shenn hene: she aaraa eh. Va'n lioar clouit 'sy vlein 1896, as va'n aaraa clouit blein er dy henney. Ayns yn aaraa, ta rolteen roish ram focklyn. “Cre'n fa ta rolteen ayns shoh?” denee Silas.

“Ta dagh rolteen soilshaghey fockle abbyrtagh,” dooyrt Rosamund. “Va ny focklyn abbyrtagh shoh ry-chlashtyn ayns un ard jeh'n ellan, as cha row ad ry-chlashtyn ayns ardjyn elley. Ta'n rolteen ginsh dhyt dy vel y fockle abbyrtagh.”

Eisht ren Rosamund loayrt mychione ny corocklyn. “Ta'n chied corockle ayns ‘mooar’, ‘bane’ as ‘poost’ ny chorockle meillagh,” dooyrt ee. “Ta shin jannoo ny corocklyn meillagh lesh ny meillyn. Tra t'ou goaill arrane, cur ny meillyn ayd ry-cheilley son dagh corockle meillagh, as bee'n arrane glen.” Ghow ny kiaulleyderyn y fockle ‘mooar’ reesht as reesht, as va'n corockle meillagh glen.

Ec jerrey yn oie, hug Silas pabyr da Rosamund. “Ta arrane noa aym,” dooyrt eh. “Ren mee eh y screeu mee shoh chaie.” Ghow ad ooilley yn arrane noa, lesh y gitar, y biol as y troorane. Va'n arrane giastyllagh as aalin. Va boggey mooar ayns y vrastyl. “T'ou giastyllagh dy mooar, Silas,” dooyrt Rosamund lesh boggey. “Ta sleih giastyllagh feer scanshoil son y Ghaelg. She boggey dooin ooilley arrane noa ayns Gaelg.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta goll dys y vrastyl?
Ta kiaulleyderyn ancheirdagh goll dys y vrastyl.
Cre ta Silas cloie?
T'eh cloie y gitar.
Cre'n fa ta rolteen roish ram focklyn?
Ta dagh rolteen soilshaghey fockle abbyrtagh.
Cre'n aght ta shin jannoo ny corocklyn meillagh?
Ta shin jannoo ad lesh ny meillyn.
Cre hug Silas da Rosamund?
Hug eh pabyr lesh arrane noa da.

lessons.title: Bee son y vashtey
lessons.summary: Mirabel Hathersage, the cook in a small café in Castletown, makes the food for a baby's christening party: her first soup is too thin so she adds potatoes, a sour apple dressing goes on a salad of bitter leaves, her helper Godfrey Pim has to smoke his cigarettes far from the door, and after the party the plates are empty, the tablecloths crumpled, and the baby's mother thanks her.
lessons.text:
Ta Mirabel Hathersage ny coagyrey ayns thie-bee beg ayns Balley Chashtal. Jesarn shoh chaie, va bashtey ayns y keeill faggys da'n thie-bee. Va lhiannoo noa ec ben aeg 'sy valley, as lurg y vashtey va ny mooinjer ooilley çheet dys y thie-bee son bee. She obbyr Mirabel bee y yannoo son y vashtey.

'Sy moghrey, ren Mirabel awree. Agh tra ghow ee y blass jeh, va'n awree thanney. “Ta'n awree shoh ro hanney,” dooyrt ee. Hug ee praaseyn stiagh 'syn awree, as lurg oor cha row'n awree thanney ny sodjey. V'eh trome as mie.

Eisht ren ee glassan. Va duillagyn glassey ayns y glassan, as va ny duillagyn castagh. “Ta ny duillagyn castagh, agh ta blass mie oc,” dooyrt Mirabel. Ren ee jough soor veih ooylyn glassey as hug ee yn jough soor er y glassan. Lesh y jough soor, cha row blass castagh ny duillagyn ro lajer.

Ta cooneyder ec Mirabel, Godfrey Pim. Ta Godfrey goaill tudjeen dagh oor. “Ny jean tudjeen y ghoaill faggys da'n dorrys jiu,” dooyrt Mirabel rish. “Bee lhiannoo aeg ayns shoh. Cha low mee tudjeen erbee faggys da'n lhiannoo.” Myr shen, hie Godfrey dys y traie son e hudjeen.

Ec mean-laa, haink ny mooinjer veih'n vashtey. Va'n lhiannoo cadley marish e voir. Hug Mirabel as Godfrey yn awree er dagh plait, as eisht y glassan. Ghow dagh peiagh yn bee dy mie. Lurg daa oor, va dagh plait follym.

Tra hie ny mooinjer thie, va ny eaddeeyn er ny buird craplit. Va dagh eaddagh craplit as fliugh. “Ta shin er craplaghey ny eaddeeyn,” dooyrt moir y lhiannoo, as ren ee gearey. “Agh va'n bee feer vie. S'mie lhien yn awree as y glassan.” Ren Godfrey ny plaityn y ghlenney, as ghow Mirabel ny eaddeeyn craplit thie marish.

Feyshtyn:
Cre'n fa va ny mooinjer çheet dys y thie-bee?
Va bashtey ayns y keeill, as va ad laccal bee lurg y vashtey.
Cre'n aght va'n chied awree?
Va'n chied awree ro hanney.
Cre'n blass va ec ny duillagyn 'sy glassan?
Va ny duillagyn castagh.
Cre'n fa hie Godfrey dys y traie?
Cha low Mirabel tudjeen erbee faggys da'n lhiannoo.
Cre'n aght va ny plaityn lurg daa oor?
Va dagh plait follym.

lessons.title: Glonney noa son y thie-glonney
lessons.summary: The glazier Alban Fothergill and his business partner Leofric Dunmore fit new windows in the glasshouse of the tree garden at St John's: the double panes hold krypton and are lighter than the old ones, Alban draws a mark at each corner, the plastic cover tears, and the gardener Winsome Tregarth explains why the plants need the light: chloroplasts in the leaves, leaves with net-like veins, seed plants and ferns, and plants that live on trees.
lessons.text:
Ta Alban Fothergill gobbraghey lesh glonney. Ta colught beg echey marish e chumraag, Leofric Dunmore. Ta'n daa chumraag gobbraghey marish y cheilley rish jeih bleeaney. 'Sy tourey shoh, t'ad cur glonney noa ayns y thie-glonney ec y garey biljagh faggys da Balley Keeill Eoin. Ta biljyn veih dagh ard jeh'n theihll 'sy garey biljagh, as ta lossreeyn aalin 'sy thie-glonney.

Ta'n glonney noa ayns daa lhieggan, as ta krypton eddyr ny daa lhieggan. “Ta'n krypton freayll y thie-glonney çheh,” dooyrt Leofric. Ta'n glonney noa eddrym neesht. Va'n shenn ghlonney trome, agh ta'n glonney noa ny s'eddrym. Ta'n daa chumraag abyl dagh glonney noa y hroggal nyn lomarcan, er yn oyr dy vel eh eddrym.

Roish y ghiarey, ren Alban mark beg ec dagh corneil jeh'n ghlonney. “Ta mark ec dagh corneil,” dooyrt eh rish Leofric. “Giare ec y vark, as bee dagh corneil kiart.” Va pabyr er y ghlonney, agh tra hrog Leofric eh, ren y pabyr raip. Ren eh raip reesht ec corneil elley, as va'n pabyr raipit ooilley. “Cha nel eh scanshoil,” dooyrt Alban. “Ta'n glonney fo'n phabyr slane.”

Haink ben y gharey, Winsome Tregarth, dy akin yn obbyr. “Ta'n glonney noa glen,” dooyrt ee. “Ta feme ec ny lossreeyn er soilshey. Ta chloroplastyn ayns dagh duillag. Ta'n chloroplast goaill y soilshey, as ta'n lus jannoo bee jeh.”

Hug ee duillag da Alban. “Jeeagh er ny cuishlinyn ayns y duillag shoh,” dooyrt ee. “T'ad moggylagh, myr moggyl. Ta cuishlinyn moggylagh ec ram lossreeyn frassagh. Ta ny lossreeyn frassagh cur magh rassyn. Agh ta ny renniee ayns shoh, as cha nel ad frassagh: cha nel rass erbee oc.”

Eisht honnick ad lus beg ard er billey 'sy thie-glonney. “She lus biljagh eh,” dooyrt Winsome. “Ta lossreeyn biljagh cummal er biljyn, as t'ad laccal soilshey ard.”

Ec jerrey yn laa, va'n glonney noa ayns dagh corneil jeh'n thie-glonney. Va'n soilshey glen er ny lossreeyn.

Feyshtyn:
Quoi ta gobbraghey marish Alban?
Ta e chumraag, Leofric Dunmore, gobbraghey marish.
Cre ta eddyr ny daa lhieggan glonney?
Ta krypton eddyr ny daa lhieggan.
Cre'n fa ren Alban mark ec dagh corneil?
Ren eh mark son giarey y ghlonney dy kiart.
Cre ta'n chloroplast jannoo?
T'eh goaill y soilshey, as ta'n lus jannoo bee jeh.
C'raad ta lossreeyn biljagh cummal?
T'ad cummal er biljyn.
Vel cuishlinyn moggylagh ec ram lossreeyn frassagh?
Ta. Ta cuishlinyn moggylagh oc.

lessons.title: Fo'n thalloo ayns Laksaa
lessons.summary: Elspeth Garnett, a guide at the old mine in Laxey, takes ten-year-old Rafe Stanhope and his dad Crispin into a tunnel: she explains how the miners broke the rock with explosives and worked in the smoke, shows them a deep pool of water where divers dive to see the old tunnels, and tells the old story of the dwarfs the miners believed lived in the rock, and Rafe tells his dad he wants to work in the mine like Elspeth.
lessons.text:
Ta Elspeth Garnett gobbraghey ec y shenn veain ayns Laksaa. Dagh laa, t'ee goaill sleih stiagh ayns thiollane fo'n thalloo. Jesarn shoh chaie, haink guilley jeih bleeaney d'eash, Rafe Stanhope, marish e ayr, Crispin.

“Jishag, jeeagh!” dooyrt Rafe, tra honnick eh y thiollane. “Ta'n thiollane shoh feer dorraghey.”

“Ta, Rafe,” dooyrt e ayr. Ren eh gearey: va Rafe gra “jishag” dagh minnid.

Hie ad stiagh 'sy thiollane lesh soilshey ayns nyn laueyn. Va'n thiollane beg as liauyr. “Ren ny obbreeyn y thiollane shoh lesh nyn laueyn as lesh stoo bleaystagh,” dooyrt Elspeth. “Va'n stoo bleaystagh brishey ny creggyn. Agh lurg dagh red bleaystagh, va jaagh mooar 'sy thiollane. Va'n jaagh dorraghey as olk son ny scowanyn. Va ny obbreeyn gobbraghey 'sy jaagh dagh laa.”

“Jishag, row'n jaagh olk son ny obbreeyn?” denee Rafe.

“Va,” dooyrt Crispin. “Va ram jeh ny obbreeyn çhing veih'n jaagh.”

Ec jerrey yn thiollane, va poyll mooar ushtey. Va'n poyll dowin as doo. “Ta'n poyll shoh feer dowin,” dooyrt Elspeth. “Ta sleih thummey 'sy phoyll dy akin ny shenn thiollaneyn fo'n ushtey. Ren daa ven thummey 'sy phoyll blein er dy henney, as hooar ad shenn greieyn ayns ny thiollaneyn shen.”

“Vod mish thummey 'sy phoyll?” denee Rafe.

“Cha nod,” dooyrt Elspeth, as ren ee gearey. “T'ou ro aeg son thummey. Agh ta skeeal aym dhyt.”

Ren Elspeth ginsh skeeal shenn da. “Va ny obbreeyn credjal dy row crivassanyn cummal 'sy chreg. Va ny crivassanyn beg, lesh folt liauyr. Tra va ny obbreeyn clashtyn red ayns ny creggyn, v'ad gra dy row ny crivassanyn gobbraghey neesht. Cha nel crivassan erbee ayn, agh she skeeal mie eh.”

Tra haink ad magh 'syn aer, dooyrt Rafe: “Jishag, ta mee laccal gobbraghey 'sy veain myr Elspeth.”

Feyshtyn:
Quoi haink dys y veain marish Rafe?
Haink e ayr, Crispin, marish.
Cre va ny obbreeyn brishey ny creggyn lesh?
V'ad brishey ny creggyn lesh stoo bleaystagh.
Cre va 'sy thiollane lurg dagh red bleaystagh?
Va jaagh mooar 'sy thiollane.
Cre ta sleih jannoo 'sy phoyll?
T'ad thummey 'sy phoyll dy akin ny shenn thiollaneyn.
Cre va ny obbreeyn credjal?
V'ad credjal dy row crivassanyn cummal 'sy chreg.
